project.name: Capstone Next
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/capstonenext` is on commit `9756055c7d37b034c218fb90e3f8e0c7fb24cd4e`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `TBEGIN` asm-writer and operand-table entries shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42475142 (capstonenext): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz_disasmnext [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42475142
bug_description.normalized: The exact 5-byte witness `6c 7c 20 05 1d` makes the fuzz harness select the PowerPC big-endian backend and pass instruction bytes `7c 20 05 1d` to `cs_disasm()`. `getInstruction()` assembles those bytes into `insn == 0x7c20051d`. In the generated PowerPC decoder, the matching `MCD_OPC_Decode, 155, 12, 71 // Opcode: TBEGIN` record is ULEB128-encoded: bytes `155, 12` decode to `Opc == 1563` (`PPC_TBEGIN`), `MCInst_setOpcode()` stores that opcode, and decode recipe 71 appends exactly one 1-bit immediate in operand slot 0. The vulnerable asm-writer metadata still gives `OpInfo0[1563] == 820308`, whose fragment-0 bits select case 18, so `printInstruction()` treats `TBEGIN` like the instructions that call `printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O)`. `printU1ImmOperand()` then reads `MCInst_getOperand(MI, 1)` even though only operand 0 was initialized. Because `MCInst_Init()` clears operand kinds and size but does not zero the union payloads of unused operands, `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal` still holds leftover stack bytes from the local `mci` object in `cs_disasm`. `printUInt32()` consumes that indeterminate value in its `val > HEX_THRESHOLD` branch, which is the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value. The fix changes the TBEGIN asm-writer entry to `263252` so fragment 0 selects case 16/operand 0, and it realigns the corresponding operand metadata in `PPCGenInstrInfo.inc`.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled instruction bytes and materializes the PowerPC instruction word that drives the vulnerable `TBEGIN` decode and print path.
source.value_from: `gt_results/arvo_42475142/poc` is the exact 5-byte witness `6c 7c 20 05 1d`. `get_platform_entry()` returns `Data[0] % platform_len()`, so `0x6c % 47 == 14` selects `platforms[14]` (`CS_ARCH_PPC`, `CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN`), and bytes 1-4 `7c 20 05 1d` are assembled here into `insn == 0x7c20051d`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. The uninitialized value loaded from `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal` reaches `printUInt32()` as `val` and is consumed by this branch.
sink.note: The saved MSan stack is `printUInt32 -> printU1ImmOperand -> printInstruction -> cs_disasm`, which matches this sink exactly.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The generated PowerPC asm-writer encodes the `TBEGIN` printer metadata as `820308`, and fragment-0 bits `(820308 >> 14) & 31 == 18` route `PPC_TBEGIN` into case 18, which prints operand slot 1. The fix changes this entry to `263252`, whose fragment-0 bits select case 16 so `TBEGIN` prints operand 0 instead.
root_cause.note: `PPCGenInstrInfo.inc` defines `PPC_TBEGIN = 1563`, so this is the `OpInfo0[1563]` entry consumed by `printInstruction()` for the decoded opcode.

tainted_value_origin.description: Stack allocation of the `MCInst` whose unused operand slots later back the uninitialized read. The saved MSan origin attributes the value to this `cs_disasm` stack frame; `MCInst_Init()` later resets operand kinds and size but does not zero `Operands[i].ImmVal` for slots that the decoder never writes.

parser_admitted.description: The witness starts with `0x6c`, so `get_platform_entry()` selects platform entry 14 (`CS_ARCH_PPC`, `CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN`), `cs_open()` creates the PPC big-endian handle, and `cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, ...)` passes the remaining four bytes `7c 20 05 1d` into the vulnerable PowerPC decoder.

fine_trace.note: Before each instruction decode, Capstone reuses the stack-allocated `mci` object. `MCInst_Init()` clears `Operands[i].Kind` and `size` but does not zero the union payloads; if a later step reads an unwritten operand slot, it observes leftover bytes from the `mci` stack allocation.
Source. For this witness the PPC big-endian branch is taken, so bytes `7c 20 05 1d` become `insn == 0x7c20051d`.
At the matching `MCD_OPC_Decode, 155, 12, 71 // Opcode: TBEGIN` table record, `decodeULEB128` interprets bytes `155, 12` as `Opc == 1563` and then reads `DecodeIdx == 71`.
The decoder resets `MI->size`, stores `MI->Opcode = 1563` (`PPC_TBEGIN`), and invokes decode recipe 71 for this instruction word.

Decode recipe 71 extracts bit 21 from `0x7c20051d` (`tmp == 1`) and appends it as the only explicit operand. After this, `MI->size == 1`, `MI->Operands[0].ImmVal == 1`, and no code has written `MI->Operands[1]`.

Because `PPC_TBEGIN = 1563`, this table entry is the printer metadata for the decoded opcode. Its fragment-0 bits are `(820308 >> 14) & 31 == 18`, so the vulnerable writer classifies `TBEGIN` as a case-18 instruction instead of the case-16/operand-0 form used by the fix (`263252`).
With `opcode == 1563`, `OpInfo0[opcode]` loads the `TBEGIN` entry from step 5, so fragment 0 evaluates to 18 and `printInstruction()` dispatches into case 18.
The case-18 arm handles `TBEGIN` in the vulnerable writer and requests operand slot 1. There is no `MCInst_getNumOperands(MI) > 1` guard before that slot is used.

With `OpNo == 1`, `MCInst_getOperand()` returns `&MI->Operands[1]` without bounds or kind checks, and `MCOperand_getImm()` reads that slot's `ImmVal`. Because step 4 initialized only operand 0 and step 0 never zeroed slot 1's union payload, this expression loads the uninitialized stack contents of `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal`.
The uninitialized operand value is forwarded unchanged to the generic unsigned printer.
Sink. `printU1ImmOperand()` passes the uninitialized `Value` into `printUInt32()`, and this branch is the first observed use that MemorySanitizer reports.

allocation_context.description: Saved MSan origin: the uninitialized value was created by stack allocation of `mci` in the `cs_disasm` frame.

format.name: raw
format.contract: An exact 5-byte binary input: `0x6c 0x7c 0x20 0x05 0x1d`. In the staged harness, this witness's first byte `0x6c` maps to platform entry 14 because `get_platform_entry()` uses `n % 47`; bytes 1-4 are the big-endian instruction word `0x7c20051d`, which reaches the vulnerable generated `TBEGIN` decode/printer path.
